full_judgment: 243. It is of the essence of the crime of abetment that abettor should assist the principal culprits towards the commission of the offence. Participation de facto may sometimes be obscure in detail, it is established by the presumption Juris et de jure that actual presence plus prior abetment can mean nothing else but participation. From the evidence of P.Ws. 3, 4,5 6, 9 and 10 that the appellant not only gave assistance, he participated in the acts of commission of the offences. When a person who abets the commission of an offence is present and helps in the commission of the offence, he is guilty of such offence. In the case of Semanza Vs.
